intro.title: Lowest Common Ancestor
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function to find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of two nodes in a binary tree. The core concept is tree traversal, where you will recursively search the tree to locate the nodes and determine their shared ancestor. You will use fundamental JavaScript constructs like functions, recursion, and conditional logic. By the end, you'll understand how to implement this common algorithm to solve problems involving hierarchical data structures.
intro.usecase: The Lowest Common Ancestor algorithm is essential in hierarchical data structures like file systems, organizational charts, and version control systems. In Git, LCA helps identify the most recent common commit when merging branches, preventing conflicts by finding where two development paths diverged. This concept also powers features in genealogy software to determine shared ancestors and in DOM tree traversal for web development, where finding common parent elements enables efficient event delegation and component communication.
